reading.title: Mechanical lubricants, gear cables and designated bike paths
reading.text: Bicycle bearing grease is a waterproof synthetic lubricant packed into wheel hubs, bottom brackets, and headsets to prevent friction wear. Stands hold bikes, and wrenches turn spokes. The mechanic applies thick green grease into the wheel bearings. A stainless-steel inner brake cable slides through outer housing to transfer hand brake lever pressure directly to the wheel brake calipers. Brake pads grip rims, and lanes guide riders. The mechanic replaces a frayed steel brake cable with a fresh wire. A dedicated off-road dirt trail winds through pine forests and rocky crests providing natural terrain for mountain biking. Bike lanes line avenues, and paths meander parks. The mountain biker navigates loose rocks along the winding singletrack trail. To execute a balanced turn on a bicycle, the rider looks through the curve, gently counters-steers, and leans the bike into the corner. Hills test stamina, and signals show intent. The cyclist slows smoothly before executing the sharp right turn. To park a bicycle is to position it upright and securely stationary in a designated municipal rack, bike corral, or storage shelter. Stops halt motion, and locks secure frames. The commuter chooses to park the bicycle outside the library entrance.
